full_judgment:
Mr. M. M. Ruhul Amin, J: This appeal by leave is directed against the judgment and order dated 20.04.2002 passed by Division Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1578 of 1993 making the Rule absolute and also the judgment and order dated 20.05.2002 passed by the High Court Division rejecting the review application summarily, filed seeking review of the judgment in the civil revision. The revisional application was filed by the plaintiff against the judgment and order dated 24.05.1993 of 6th Court of Addition District Judge, Dhaka, passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No.45 of 1993 reversing the judgment and order dated 20.02.1993 dismissing the Miscellaneous Case No.28 of 1991 registered under Order 9 Rule 13 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The Miscellaneous Case was filed seeking setting aside of the ex parte decree dated 12.12.1984.

2. Short facts are that the respondents' predecessor filed Title Suit No.208 of 1984 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Dhaka for declaration of title in the land described in the schedule of the plaint and for further declaration that the Memo No.560 dated 09.06.1984 issued by the defendant No.6 (Sub Divisional Engineer, P.W.D., Sub-Division No.1 Tejgaon Industrial Area, Dhaka) is illegal, unlawful, without jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiff.

3. The defendants entered appearance in the said suit and prayed for time to file written statement but ultimately no written statement having been filed the suit was fixed for ex parte hearing on 06.11.1984. On that date the defendants prayed for time to file written statement but no written statement was filed and the suit was fixed on 28.11.1984 for ex parte hearing. The date so fixed for ex parte hearing was shifted to 12.12.1984 by the Court and on that date the suit was heard ex parte and decreed. Thereafter the defendants filed an application under Order 9 Rule 13 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure and thereupon the aforementioned Miscellaneous Case was stated. The prayer for restoration of the original suit to its file and number was opposed by the plaintiff. The trial court dismissed the case holding that the petitioners of the miscellaneous case failed to make out a case for setting aside the ex parte decree. Thereupon the defendants took an appeal being Miscellaneous Appeal No.45 of 1993 before the District Judge, Dhaka. The appeal was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, 6th Court, Dhaka and the same was alloyed and the ex parte decree dated a 12/12.1984 was set aside and the original shit was restored to file and number. The plaintiff then moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction and obtained Rule. The High Court Division made the Rule absolute upon observing that the appellate court was in error in not holding that the defendants were guilty of latches in conducting their case and thereupon caused failure of justice in allowing the miscellaneous appeal. As against the order dated 20.04.2002 of the High Court Division making the Rule absolute the appellants filed an application under Order 47 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil procedure seeking review of the aforesaid judgment and order and the High Court Division by the order dated 20.05.2002 rejected the review application summarily upon observing that no case for review was made out.

4. Leave was granted to consider the submission that the entire suit plot No.533 was acquired by the Government and the respondent No.1 obtained the ex parte decree by making false statement on the basis of forged document and as such the impugned judgments and orders dated 20.04.2002 and 20.05.2002 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.1578 of 1993 are liable to be set aside for ends of justice and further submission that the respondent No.1 previously filed a suit being Title Suit No.222 of 1979 against the present appellants for the same relief and the same was dismissed for default and the respondent No.1 having not filed any Miscellaneous Case or appeal against the said order dated 05.03.1975 the present suit has been filed suppressing the said facts in could ex parte decree was also obtained and as such the impugned judgment and order dated 20.04.2002 and 20.05.2002 passed in Civil Revision No.1578 of 1993 are liable to be set aside.

5. We have heard Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali, the learned Attorney General for the appellants and Mr. T. H. Khan, the learned Counsel for respondent Nos. 1-3 and perused the judgment of the High Court Division and other connected papers.

<u>6. It is not disputed that by gazette notification dated 20.02.1950 the total area of C. S. Plot No.533 (suit plot) i.e. 2.30 acres of Mouza-Tejkunipara. P.S. Tejgaon. District-Dhaka along with other lands were acquired by the Government.</u>

7. The plaintiff's case is that although Suit Plot No.533 was requisitioned by the Government in L.A. Case No.3 of 1948-49 but subsequently the suit plot was released from such requisition on 20.02.1950 which fact would be evident from a memorandum vide memo No.5463 dated 18.12.1988 of the Additional Land Acquisition Officer, Dhaka.

8. The learned Attorney General submits that after final publication of gazette notification dated 20.02.1950 the right, title and interest if any, of the original owner in the acquired land including the suit plot had already extinguished and once the property was acquired and gazette notification published, the same vested in the government and cannot be released in the manner as claimed by plaintiff. In support of his argument the learned Attorney General cited the case of Director of Housing & Settlement Vs. Abdul Majid Howlader and others reported in 9 MLR (AD) 73 and submitted that in that case it was held that the settled law is that upon acquisition of particular property the same vests in the Government and that being the position in law the prayer for release made by the Respondents was totally misconceived one since under the law they were not entitled to have the property released. Accordingly suit so filed seeking release of the property was not legally well advised one as well as was not entertainable in law. He further submitted that in the instant case the validity of acquisition of the property in question has not been disputed. He next submitted that the undisputed position is that the property in suit was acquired under the provision of (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 and to that respect gazette notification has been published making the acquisition final and vesting the property in suit in the Government. As per provision of law on the publication of the gazette notification the property acquired vests in the Government and consequent thereupon Government becomes the owner of the property. The person whose property is acquired under the Act and consequent thereupon vests in the Government, is not entitled to claim any interest in the land so acquired. In that view of the matter there was no scope for the plaintiffs, who have no interest of any kind in the land in suit, to seek for a declaration that they are entitled to get the property released.

9. The learned Counsel for respondent Nos.1-3 submitted that the Executive Engineer, P.W.D. Development Division-1, Dhaka vide memo No.615 dated 21.01.1950 recommended for release of the all lands out of alignment and accordingly notice under Rule 10(2) of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Rules, 1948 was issued. The learned Counsel has also drawn our attention to the order sheet of L.A. Case No.3 of 1948-49 dated 20.12.1949 and submitted that the Executive Engineer, P.W.D. by his memo No.10352-58D dated 19.12.1949 sent a revised blue print showing the land to be acquired permanently and temporarily and accordingly by order dated 12.01.1950 after obtaining a report from kanango of the office of the Deputy Commissioner, the Requisition Branch of the Revenue Department of the then Government of East Pakistan was written for action to be taken on the revised plan received from the Executive Engineer, Public Works Department. Order dated 07.03.1950 of the same L.A. Case is as follows:-

"De-requisition notices served. Fresh notice under section 5(7) in form 'D' has been re-submitted to Government with T.O. No.96-L.A. dated 21.01.1950 for publication. Wait till 25.03.1950.

Sd/-Illegible

L. A. C."

10. It is on record that gazette notification regarding permanent acquisition of the land was published on 20.02.1950 as noticed earlier and as such the de-requisition or release of the property as claimed by the e plaintiff could not take place. Therefore, the plaintiff cannot take any advantage of the order sheet of L.A. Case No.3 of 1948-49 or the correspondence made between different Government functionaries in this respect for before these correspondence could reach finality the Gazette notification dated 20.02.1950 regarding acquisition of the suit land was published.

11. It is the case of the plaintiff that 30 decimals of land suit Plot No.533 was under acquisition and the remaining 2 acres of land was outside acquisition as per revised blue print prepared by the Executive Engineer, Development Division No.1, P.W.D. and according to plaintiff's own case steps were taken for de-requisitioning and releasing the remaining 2 acres of land which the plaintiff tried to show from the order sheet of L.A. Case No.3 of 1948/49 as noted earlier.

12. From the plaint of Title Suit No.208 of 1984 of the 1st  Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka brought by Mrs. Shamirunnessa Bibi wife of Hasan Ali against Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka and others it appears that the plaintiff sought declaration of her title over the entire 2.30 acres of land of C .S. Plot No.533 of C. S. Khatian No.112 of Mouza Tejkunipara, P.S. Tejgaon, Dhaka although according to plaintiffs own case 30 decimals of land was under acquisition,

13. Without going into the merit of the matter it can be safely said that when it is the admitted case of the plaintiff that 30 decimals of land out of 2.30 acres of land of Suit Plot No.533 is within the acquired land of the Government as per gazette notification dated 20.02.1950, the plaintiff's suit for entire 2.30 acres of Plot No.533 on the face of it was not maintainable. Being faced with the situation the learned Counsel for the respondents could not give a satisfactory reply on this point.

<u>14. The learned Attorney General in this connection submitted that to avoid the embargo of section 14A of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948, the plaintiff brought the suit claiming the entire 2.30 acres of land of Suit Plot No.533. The plaintiff also sought correction of record of right in respect of entire 2.30 acres of land although she claims 100 acres of land only and not the entire 2.30 acres. The learned Attorney General further submitted that although the plaintiff cleverly sought declaration of title over the entire 2.00 acres of land of the suit plot but that will not bring the suit out of the mischief of section 14A of the Act.</u>

15. The learned Attorney General lastly argued that in this court in exercise of the power conferred under Article104 of the Constitution can do complete justice and dispose of the matter finally. In support of his contention the learned Attorney General cited the cases of Gannysons Ltd. Vs. Sonali Bank reported in 37 DLR (AD) 42, AFM Naziruddin Vs. Mrs. Hameeda Banu reported in 45 DLR (AD) 38 and Secretary, Internal Resources Division, Ministry of Finance and Chairman, National Board of Revenue, Dhaka Vs. Nasrin Banu and 5 others reported in 48 DLR (AD) 171.

<u>16. We have already noticed that in this case ex-parte decree was passed on 12.12.1984 in Title Suit No.208 of 1993 and in Miscellaneous Appeal No.45 of 1993 the Ex-parte decree was set aside and the original suit was restored to file and number. The High Court Division making the Rule absolute in the revisional application restored the ex-parte decree to its original position. Therefore, the fact remains that there was no contested hearing of the suit and the defendants could not place their case and other materials before the court for proper adjudication.</u>

17. Complete justice is to be done in an appropriate case. "It is an extraordinary procedure for doing justice for completion of or putting an end to a cause or matter pending before this court. If a substantial justice under law and on undisputed facts can be made so that parties may not be pushed to further litigation, then a recourse to the provision of Article 104 may be justified" (45 D.L.R. (AD)38)

18. Therefore, in the circumstances of the case, we do not consider it a fit case to do complete justice.

<u>19. Since there are some patent incongruities in the plaint of Title Suit No.208 of 1994 brought by the plaintiff Samirunnessa Bibi as noticed earlier the ex parte decree dated 12.12.1984 ex-facie is not sustainable.</u>

20. Accordingly the learned Additional District Judge did not commit any illegality in allowing the Miscellaneous Appeal No.45 of 1993 rather the High Court Division was in error in making the Rule absolute.

21. The appeal is, therefore, allowed without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment of the High Court Division is set aside and those of the appellate court passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No.45 of 1993 are restored.

End.
